subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@fintechco.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Sara / Luis —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the time. Quick recap of the performance items we discussed and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the perf test: 

Summary of current targets (from call):
- Latency: 99th pctl generation target <= 350 ms end-to-end (network + inference) for standard chat flows.
- p95 (interactive chat) target: ~200 ms is ideal for FintechCo but p99 goal above.
- Throughput: baseline 300 requests/sec sustained, with burst to 600 rps for peak windows.
- Concurrency: expect ~150 concurrent active sessions; design for 200 concurrency headroom.
- Streaming: required for low-latency UX (token-by-token streaming to clients).
- Payloads: median prompt size ~120 tokens; worst-case ~1,200 tokens for long history replays.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) We’ll share the SLO checklist and perf test plan (attached). Please confirm the two most important decision criteria (latency p95/p99, throughput/concurrency) you want measured.
2) Redwood SE (Rishi) will run an initial simulated workload against a non-production endpoint the week of Aug 10 — please confirm a 2-3 hour test window.
3) We’ll run both streaming and non-streaming scenarios and provide a breakdown by token-level cost and latency distribution.
4) Post-test: we’ll share the raw metrics + suggested runtime config (batching, quantization profile, KV cache policy) to meet your targets.

Attachments: fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx, perf_test_plan.csv
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/slo-checklist

Open items for you to confirm:
- Is p95 <= 200 ms a hard booking requirement or an aspirational target?
- Do you have any hard limits on 99th percentile latency?
- Any restrictions on network egress or private VPC-only testing?

Happy to jump on a 15m sync with Rishi and your infra lead to lock test window.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 17:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks, Marissa — great session. A few clarifications from our side: 

- p95 <= 200 ms: this is what our product team calls 'interactive' and is close to a hard requirement for chat features. If your p95 is higher, it may degrade product adoption.
- p99: we'd like to see <= 400 ms for most flows, but we understand extreme edge cases can be higher.
- Throughput/Concurrency: we currently expect 300 rps sustained with 500 rps burst. Concurrency target is 200.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the chat product (token-by-token). Falling back to non-streaming would be a last resort.

A few asks before we schedule the perf run:
1) Can you confirm whether the streaming endpoint will use HTTP/2 server-sent events or gRPC? We prefer HTTP/2 for our client stack.
2) What batching strategy does Redwood recommend for our workload? E.g., dynamic batching with a 20 ms latency cap vs fixed micro-batches.
3) Will you include quantized model variants in the test (e.g., 4-bit) so we can see cost/latency trade-offs?

We can do a 2-3 hour window on Aug 11 or Aug 12 (PDT) in the afternoon; please propose a concrete slot.

-Sara
Head of Product, Messaging
FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@fintechco.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 18:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Sara — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and confirmation of next steps: 

1) Streaming protocol: we can support HTTP/2 streaming (SSE) for the demo/test. Our runtime exposes both HTTP/2 streaming and WebSocket paths; for your stack HTTP/2 SSE is the simplest.
2) Batching strategy: default recommendation is dynamic batching with a 15-25 ms latency cap for interactive traffic — we’ll show metrics for both 20 ms and 50 ms caps during the test.
3) Quantized variants: yes — we’ll include a 4-bit quantized model option and a float16 baseline so you can compare latency and cost.

I’ve attached the SLO checklist and perf test plan. Rishi will own the test orchestration; looping him in now. Proposed windows: 
- Wed, Aug 11 13:00-16:00 PDT (preferred)
- Thu, Aug 12 14:00-17:00 PDT (backup)

Drive link again: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/slo-checklist

Rishi / Aditya — can you confirm the test harness plan and whether we need any customer-provided test credentials or a specific VPC setup?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Johnson <sara.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2026 02:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Sara / team —

Thanks for the details. Below is the proposed test harness and scenarios we plan to run; happy to adjust based on your infra constraints.

Test harness overview:
- Endpoint: non-prod streaming endpoint (HTTP/2 SSE) hosted in us-west-2.
- Auth: short-lived API key we’ll provision; if you prefer VPC peering we can run inside the customer VPC but that adds setup time.
- Payload sizes: median prompt ~120 tokens (approx 600 bytes), long-history tests up to 1,200 tokens.
- Models: baseline float16 and 4-bit quantized variant.
- Batching: dynamic batching with 20 ms cap, and a 50 ms cap run for comparison.

Scenarios to run (2.5 hours total):
1) Interactive streaming (45m): steady 200 concurrent streams, 300 rps sustained, 600 rps bursts. Metrics: token latency distribution, p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, error rates.
2) Bulk inference (30m): non-streaming batched throughput test to characterize max rps.
3) Long-history replay (30m): larger payloads to validate memory/KV cache impact.
4) Failure & fallbacks (15m): simulate model switch and network blips to verify graceful degradation.
5) Cost/latency comparison (30m): run float16 vs 4-bit quantized to provide cost per 1k tokens and latency deltas.

Deliverables post-test: raw logs, latency percentiles by scenario, per-token cost estimates, recommended runtime config (batch size, quant profile, cache TTLs).

Questions for FintechCo prior to test:
- Can you confirm whether we should use HTTP/2 SSE or gRPC? Marissa noted you prefer HTTP/2.
- Will you provide a test API key and a sample request generator, or should we run traffic from our harness hitting your client-side endpoints?
- Any egress/VPC requirements (e.g., must be inside your private network)?

Proposed test slot: Wed, Aug 11 13:00 PDT. If that works, I’ll schedule and send calendar invites with the test plan and required credentials checklist.
